head: 5e23fa5afaa9d8f8f5a957c45a761edd1d64e516
claim: An installed OpenCode login with a detected store is listed honestly as unknown and can be launched with the person’s HOME and no BYOKit folder or XDG overrides; missing store or binary means no row.

steps.start: Synthetic OpenCode binary and auth.json in a disposable HOME; no real login or network
steps: List installed accounts with the synthetic OpenCode binary and login-store path present; observe installed-opencode with unknown status and the non-secret-check reason.
Launch the installed account and run the supplied binary with the returned environment; observe HOME preserved, the six per-use overrides removed, and no folder or XDG override.
List again with the store missing, the binary missing, and installed discovery disabled; observe no installed OpenCode row in each case.
steps.result: The installed OpenCode account is listed only with its binary and store, stays honestly unknown, and launches with the user HOME and no BYOKit folder overrides.

verdicts.seen: I read the whole capture: one list entry, one launch entry, and one guards entry covering three negative cases. The list line shows "installed-opencode; state unknown because OpenCode has no non-secret sign-in check", matching the unknown state for an installed login. The launch line shows "HOME preserved, no folder/XDG overrides, and all six per-use overrides removed", matching the HOME-only launch. The guards line says "missing store, missing binary, and installed:false each produce no installed OpenCode row", matching the no-row cases. The result line reads PASS. The outcome names a single part, so parts and covers are empty.
